cli.browser.pairing_code: Your Local Operator pairing code is {code}.
cli.browser.enter_code: Switch to Chrome: a Local Operator tab is open there with a box for the code. Type the code and press Pair.
cli.browser.enter_each_code: Each browser now has a Local Operator tab open. Type the first code there and press Pair. If it says the code didn''t match, type the other code instead.
cli.browser.enter_each_code_icon: In each browser, click the Local Operator icon in the toolbar (it may be under the puzzle-piece icon). Have the codes in front of you first: the box closes if you click away. Type the first code and press Pair. If it says the code didn''t match, type the other code instead.
cli.browser.already_paired: Your browser is already paired with Local Operator, so no code is needed. To pair another browser, install the Local Operator extension there, then ask Local Operator to "pair my browser" again.
cli.browser.no_extension_waiting: No Local Operator extension is connected yet, so there is no code to show. Open Chrome and check that the Local Operator extension is installed and turned on: https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/local-operator/omibaecbjdhgbbcedbnnnmjpmopfheof It connects within a minute. Then ask Local Operator to "pair my browser" again.

cli.browser.no_tabs_unknown: No ownership records. The bridge did not answer, so open tabs are unknown — run 'lop browser status' to check the daemon.
cli.browser.cleanup_closed: Browser cleanup: closed. The tab was closed and its record settled.
cli.browser.cleanup_pending: Browser cleanup: pending — nothing was closed ({detail}). Retry the same command once the bridge answers; the generation you copied is still current.
cli.browser.enter_code_icon: In Chrome, click the Local Operator icon in the toolbar (it may be under the puzzle-piece icon). Have the code in front of you first: the box closes if you click away. Type the code and press Pair.
cli.browser.pair_no_page_hint: No tab? Click the Local Operator icon in Chrome''s toolbar (it may be under the puzzle-piece icon) and type it there.
cli.browser.pair_code_lifetime: The code works for {minutes, plural, one {# minute} other {# minutes}}. After pairing, Local Operator asks you in Chrome to Allow each new website the first time it visits one.
cli.browser.pair_several_header: More than one browser is waiting to pair. Each has its own code:
cli.browser.pair_outdated: The browser marked {label} has an older Local Operator extension. It can still pair, but some features need version {want}. To update it, type chrome://extensions in Chrome''s address bar, turn on Developer mode (top right), then click Update.
cli.browser.pair_no_daemon: Local Operator can''t talk to your browser right now. Run ''lop browser install'' to fix that, then ''lop browser pair'' again.
cli.browser.pair_unreachable: Local Operator couldn''t reach your browser. Run ''lop browser restart'', then ''lop browser pair'' again. (Details: {detail})
cli.browser.pair_after_reset: Browsers unpaired. In a few seconds, run ''lop browser pair'' to get a new code.
